subject: Urgent: Noventa - recurring tail latency on long-window requests (p95/p99 regressions)
messages:
From: Emily Cho <support@noventa.ai>
To: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Mar 2028 22:12:05 -0700
Subject: Spike in tail latency for multi-doc summarization (8k-16k requests)

Michael —

We started seeing a big increase in tail latencies yesterday evening for our nightly processing: p95 has jumped from ~420ms to ~1.5s, and p99 is now frequently >4s for requests that submit 8k–16k context windows. Throughput is also dropping because many requests time out and get retried. Attached is our internal sampling and the request IDs we captured. We’re on a tight launch cadence and this is blocking a partner demo Friday.

Can Redwood confirm whether this is an active regression or saturation on your hosted tier? We tried pinning to the smallest compatible model and reducing batch sizes but the tail persists.

— Emily
Senior Integrations, Noventa AI

Attachments: noventa_latency_report_q1.csv, req_ids.txt
From: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.com>
To: Emily Cho <support@noventa.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Mar 2028 22:45:19 -07:00
Subject: Re: Spike in tail latency for multi-doc summarization (8k-16k requests)

Emily — thanks for the quick signal and the traces. We see matching error bursts and p99 spikes on our hosted API for the tenant ID you included.

What we've done so far:
- Ingested your sample traces and matched request IDs to backend logs
- Scoped the spike to long-window requests (predominantly 8k–16k lengths) with high KV cache churn
- Short-term mitigation: enabled stricter routing to fall back to the low-latency variant for your tenant to reduce tail, but that increases cost and slightly lowers generation quality on edge cases

I'm escalating to product and eng ops now. If you can share 3 representative request IDs with full payloads we can run them head-to-head in a repro environment.

— Michael
Director, Customer Success, Redwood Inference

Attachments: req_trace_2028-03-21.zip
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Mar 2028 00:08:33 -07:00
Subject: Re: Spike in tail latency for multi-doc summarization (8k-16k requests)

Looping infra/serving folks — initial triage notes from runtime traces:
- The p95/p99 jump correlates with increased KV cache eviction rates when sequence lengths exceed ~6k tokens; long-window requests cause higher memory churn which occasionally forces a synchronous KV reload path, adding 600–1200ms to tail cases
- There were two kernel scheduling stalls on the GPU host pool servicing the hosted tier between 21:45–23:10 PDT; not all long-window requests hit those hosts but tenant routing decisions placed a subset there during a localized rolling deploy
- Error-rate increase (5xx spiking from 0.3% -> 2.7%) appears in requests that hit the synchronous fallback path under memory pressure

Immediate ask for eng: pin affected tenant away from the impacted host pool, enable agressive KV prefetch for their tenant, and temporarily limit max_context to 16k at the gateway to avoid pathological churn.

Neha
Sr. Product Manager, Serving Runtime
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Mar 2028 08:26:04 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Spike in tail latency — elevating to execs and ops

Team — I’ve flagged this as an executive action item given impact to launch. Rishi, we need a quick assessment: impact window, mitigation timeline, and whether we need to issue a customer-facing credit or SLA exception. Please prepare a one-page incident brief for the CTO and CRO by 10:30 PDT.

High-level risks to call out:
- If tail persists we risk the Noventa demo and potential escalation to procurement, which could delay their expansion (Deal-4721).
- Broadly, this strain on hosted routing for long-window workloads could affect other tenants if routing policy funnels too many heavy requests to a single pool.

Laura
VP, Sales Operations
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Mar 2028 09:14:41 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Spike in tail latency — elevating to execs and ops

Planned actions (timeline):
- 09:30 PDT: evac tenant routing from impacted host pool and reassign to warm pool (done)
- 10:00 PDT: enable tenant-scoped KV prefetch and increase cache windows; monitor p95/p99 in real time (in progress)
- 11:00 PDT: deploy a targeted kernel scheduling fix to reduce synchronous stalls by removing a defensive memory fence in the long-window path (requires canary)
- 15:00 PDT: decision point on whether to throttle max_context to 12k for hosted tier vs. pushing a safer but slower fix; if throttling, method will be applied via routing policy with a 24-hour opt-out window for enterprise tenants

Recommendation for commercial: offer Noventa a one-time service credit for the outage window and priority engineering support for their Friday demo. Need sales sign-off to formalize.

Rishi
Head of Serving Runtime Engineering
From: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.com>
To: Emily Cho <support@noventa.ai>, David Osei <ctm@noventa.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Mar 2028 16:40:12 -07:00
Subject: Update: mitigation in place for Noventa long-window tail latency

Emily / David — quick update from Redwood: we identified a localized scheduling regression on a subset of hosted GPU hosts that, combined with high KV cache churn from 8k–16k contexts, produced the observed p95/p99 regressions and increased retry rates.

What we’ve done for Noventa (effective 10:00 PDT):
- Re-routed your tenant off the impacted host pool to a warm pool with lower eviction rates
- Enabled tenant-scoped KV prefetch and widened cache windows for your workload
- Deployed a canary fix to reduce kernel stalls (monitoring closely for regression)

Initial signal: p95 dropped from ~1.5s -> ~430ms within the first 20 minutes; p99 is trending down but we’ll keep the temporary routing in place for 24 hours while we validate.

Commercial proposal: offer a one-time credit equivalent to 2 days of hosted overage and a private debug session before your Friday demo. Please confirm whether that is acceptable and share any additional trace IDs if you see further issues.

— Michael
Director, Customer Success, Redwood Inference
